leak_test_details:
Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/83a4d5f8-8137-5cb1-9baa-8ac55fed2a66/scratchpad/ml/verify_priors/leak.js. Outputs: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/83a4d5f8-8137-5cb1-9baa-8ac55fed2a66/scratchpad/ml/verify_priors/out/leak_<season>.out.

Seasons 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25, rounds 5, 12, 20 and 33 (12 cases). For each case I built a truncated copy of the season:
- dropped all hist rows with round >= r;
- marked fixtures of round >= r unfinished, with no score;
- set every numeric player column after the first 8 to null, keeping 'code';
- set events so that r is the next event and later rounds are unfinished;
- attached the experiment's priors_<season>.json as d.priors.

Round r was given only stats-free stubs (round, opponent, home flag, fixture id) so the replay knows which players are targets and which club they play for. I computed predictions two ways: (a) btRound on the truncated data, and (b) the production path pmPredictAll on live-like truncated data (player totals = sums of the truncated history, p.code taken from cols, so priors are found the way the site would find them). I compared both with the full-data btRun predictions for round r.

Result: all 12 cases PASS. 381 to 425 players per round, 0 missing, 0 extra, max abs diff 0.0 on both paths, and no rows from round >= r left in the data. The priors were active in these cases: 273 to 332 target players per round had a prior entry in 2023-24 and 2024-25. 2022-23 has no priors.

Positive control: I planted a leak (end-of-season minutes from d.rows added into pPlay0) in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/83a4d5f8-8137-5cb1-9baa-8ac55fed2a66/scratchpad/ml/verify_priors/leaky_control.js. The test caught it (FAIL, max diff 0.78 and 0.62), so it is sensitive.

The truncation test cannot catch a leak inside the priors file itself, because both sides read the same priors. I checked that part by code reading and data comparison:
- build_priors.js uses prev = ALL.slice(0, ti), i.e. strictly earlier seasons only.
- The target season file is loaded only for its team code list, and only for the relegated-sides fallback, which is disabled (TR = TRP = 0).
- In priors_2024-25.json, all 570 ago=1 entries match 2023-24 minutes totals, and only 4 match 2024-25 totals (coincidences). All 554 ago=2 entries match 2022-23.
- My rebuilt priors files are byte-identical to the shipped ones.
other_leakage_or_protocol_issues:
No leakage or protocol violation found.

Diff of model.js against fp_model.js:
- The edits are limited to the PM constants, the optional team prior in pmCtx (disabled), extra per-90 evidence in shr/fin inside pmPlayer, the PK pseudo-matches in pPlay0, q60 and ePlay, and passing code in btRound.
- No use of the current season's end-of-season totals, final prices, now_cost, the xP column, same-round rows, or 2025-26 data.
- Previous-season end-of-season totals are used, which the README allows because those seasons are complete.
- PWD = 0 gives a weight of exactly 0 for ago = 2 entries (Math.pow(0, 1) = 0), so 2022-23 data does not enter 2024-25 rates.

Tuning:
- All 47 grid runs in exp_priors/logs/grid1-7.jsonl are on 2023-24 only. None are on 2024-25.
- No learned model is involved.
- I found no evidence of more than the 1 declared validation look, although that cannot be fully proven from the files.

Caveats (not violations):
- PW and PK were tuned on a single train season. 2022-23 equals the baseline by construction because it has no previous season.
- The validation gain is small and not clearly significant. Paired per round on 2024-25: mean gain 0.0041 MAE, standard error 0.0029, the model beats the baseline in 19 of 35 rounds. Compare the claimed 32 of 35 on train 2023-24.
- DEF gets worse on validation (1.678 to 1.693) and FWD is flat. The experiment discloses both.
- I ran an equivalent of reproduce.sh inside verify_priors/ instead of the original. The original rewrites files in exp_priors/, which I was told not to modify.
notes:
The analysis is finished. Verdict: confirmed. The numbers reproduce exactly, the leak test passed in all 12 cases, and I found no protocol issue.

**1. Reproduction**
I rebuilt the priors with a copy of build_priors.js in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/83a4d5f8-8137-5cb1-9baa-8ac55fed2a66/scratchpad/ml/verify_priors/ and the files came out byte-identical to the shipped ones. I then ran my own baseline.js-style evaluator (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/83a4d5f8-8137-5cb1-9baa-8ac55fed2a66/scratchpad/ml/verify_priors/eval.js) with exp_priors/model.js.

| Season | Model MAE | Bias | Baseline MAE (fp_model.js) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2022-23 (train) | 1.695102 | -0.3215 | 1.6951 |
| 2023-24 (train) | 1.743902 | -0.0021 | 1.7659 |
| 2024-25 (validation) | 1.689737 | 0.0473 | 1.6936 |

All numbers, including by-position MAE, match the claims to full precision. Setting PW = PK = 0 gives exactly the production numbers.

**2. Leak test:** passed in all 12 cases. Details are in leak_test_details.

**3. Code and protocol:** no issues. Details are in other_leakage_or_protocol_issues.

**Caution:** the validation improvement is real but small and only weakly supported (-0.0038 MAE; per round 0.0041 ± 0.0029, 19 of 35 rounds better). PW and PK were tuned on 2023-24 alone, and DEF predictions get worse on validation.
